thread:
kevin-cs: FYI Sable reporting sustained 429s + 500ms+ p95 after their paid campaign landed around 09:10 UTC. Dedicated pool dp-sable-03. They say baseline ~220 qps, burst to ~1800 qps. Customer expects no throttles. Can we triage? :wave:

maria-support: Ack, opening a ticket with them. Any quick indicators (throttles vs autoscale lag vs auth)? Asking for 1h graphs and the exact window.

sanjay-eng: Initial look — autoscaler didn't add replicas fast enough. From metrics (09:10-09:25): GPU util across replicas jumped from 35% -> 92%, queue length spiked. Pool config currently:

```
pool_id: dp-sable-03
min_replicas: 2
max_replicas: 8
target_gpu_utilization: 0.6
scale_cooldown_seconds: 120
scale_policy: per_gpu
```

We hit max_replicas at ~09:14 and started returning 429s. Also seeing a small subset of replicas with sustained high latency (noisy neighbor?).

aj-infra: +1 on noisy neighbor. Node host ip 10.12.4.21 shows one container doing large batching for another tenant (tenant-id: tenant-omega). That job pushed memory to 95% and triggered memory reclaim which increased GC/paging in other containers. Found these lines in node logs:

```
[09:11:53] container tenant-omega batcher: open files=10240, memory=48GB
[09:12:07] kernel: OOM-kill suspect
[09:12:10] container dp-sable-03 replica-3: slow-kernel-io, preempted
```

I can repro locally-ish by running a 1k concurrent `curl` flood against a cheap model on that pool: `ab -n 2000 -c 1000 http://dp-sable-03.redwood.internal/v1/generate` — you'll see 429s once max_replicas reached.

maria-support: Customer also reported auth errors intermittently. Logs show some 401s for a small fraction of requests around the same time. Might be unrelated token rotation retries.

tara-ops: Autoscaler logs show repeated backoff attempts: `scale_decision=scale_up desired_replicas=12 reason="cpu/gpu_util > threshold"` then `backoff=exponential delay=30s` until hitting max_replicas. There's a separate cooldown window of 120s in config which slowed catch-up. Also saw thermal/policy throttles on that host (we're hitting host-level limits because tenant-omega spawned large batch jobs). Snippet:

```
[09:12:20] autoscaler: desired=12 -> clamped=8 (max)
[09:12:20] autoscaler: cooldown active, delaying further scale actions
[09:13:05] node 10.12.4.21: host-cgroup throttle active, migrating pods
```

luke-sre: Short term mitigations to propose now:
- Increase `max_replicas` to 16 for dp-sable-03 to give headroom (quick fix).
- Temporarily route 20% of traffic to hosted fallback model for Sable via routing policy.
- Quarantine tenant-omega workload on its own node pool to eliminate noisy neighbor.

Commands I'm about to run (need 👍 from infra):
```
redwood-cli pools update dp-sable-03 --max-replicas 16 --scale-cooldown 30
redwood-cli routes update sable-production --split 80:20 --fallback hosted-gpt-medium
```

aj-infra: 👍 on quarantine, but need change window. I'll cordon 10.12.4.21 and migrate tenant-omega. Also will pin tenant-omega's batch jobs to a separate shard.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: autoscaler-config-change applied to dp-sable-03 by luke-sre at 2026-03-17T09:20:03Z :rocket:

support-bot: billing-note: Sable is on a reserved pool contract with headroom to scale; we will apply short-term overage credits for this incident per SRE playbook.

kevin-cs: Thanks. Follow-ups: (1) confirm migration of tenant-omega and that 429s stop, (2) set target utilization for dedicated pools at 50% for customer-facing tenants to avoid this headroom problem, (3) run a postmortem and capacity plan for Sable with baseline/peak numbers.

maria-support: Told customer we increased capacity and quarantined noisy tenant; they can keep campaign running while we monitor. They're looping in their infra: sable-platform@sable.co.

sanjay-eng: Action items:
- Run a synthetic load test reproducer at 11:00 UTC that mimics their 1.8k qps burst (script + exact headers from customer).
- Add a Canary routing policy for high-QPS traffic.
- Update pool defaults to `target_gpu_utilization: 0.5` for public/merchant customers.

aj-infra: I've started cordon/drain on 10.12.4.21, migration in progress. Expect <10m to finish.

luke-sre: I'll draft a short postmortem and recommended sizing table: baseline qps -> min_replicas, peak qps -> headroom multiplier (x2 for marketing bursts).

kevin-cs: Closing loop — if throttles persist after migration, escalate to ENG-ML for kernel-level investigation. For now monitoring shows p95 latency down to 220ms and 429s back to <0.1%. :thumbsup:

maria-support: Customer acknowledged. We'll follow-up with postmortem and billing credit details. :white_check_mark:
